body:
The bundled manufacturer OUI files were corrupt:

- Every line of [`texas_instruments.txt`](https://github.com/dpep/rspec-networking/blob/0e7e7cb/lib/rspec/networking/mac_address/texas_instruments.txt#L1) had a `mac_addresses.tsv:` grep prefix, so `from("texas instruments")` never matched.
- Several files had their leading zeros stripped by a spreadsheet. For example, Microsoft's `002248` was stored as [`2248`](https://github.com/dpep/rspec-networking/blob/0e7e7cb/lib/rspec/networking/mac_address/microsoft.txt#L19). The hardcoded [Xerox `000000` entry](https://github.com/dpep/rspec-networking/blob/0e7e7cb/lib/rspec/networking/mac_address_manufacturers.rb#L6) was papering over one case of this.
- `apple.txt` and `zyxel.txt` each contained a currency string (`AED 645.00`, `BEF 107.00`).
- The lists were stale; Apple, for example, had 1270 entries against 1593 in the registry now.

The new [`script/update_manufacturers`](https://github.com/dpep/rspec-networking/blob/264608b/script/update_manufacturers#L13) regenerates the files from the [IEEE OUI registry](https://standards-oui.ieee.org/), using only [MA-L assignments](https://github.com/dpep/rspec-networking/blob/264608b/script/update_manufacturers#L30). Its output includes every well-formed old entry except 3 old "Texas Instruments" rows that actually belong to Texas Memory Systems, Texas Microsystems and Texas Digital Systems.

[`mac_address_manufacturers.rb`](https://github.com/dpep/rspec-networking/blob/264608b/lib/rspec/networking/mac_address_manufacturers.rb) now just loads the files. A new [spec](https://github.com/dpep/rspec-networking/blob/264608b/spec/mac_address_manufacturers_spec.rb) checks that every entry is 6 uppercase hex digits; it fails on the old data.
